answer: Picture a dune of fake agents: each one must pass a fresh, unique task every epoch, graded by random peers, before earning anything. Like a lotus that opens only in sunlight, rewards open only to real work. An attacker running 1,000 sybils pays for 1,000 separate inference runs and risks umber-stained reputations when graders spot clones, so the cost scales linearly with every fake.
